text.awadhi:
संकर सुवन केसरी नंदन।
तेज प्रताप महा जग बंदन॥
text.telugu:
సంకర సువన కేసరీ నందన।
తేజ ప్రతాప మహా జగ బందన॥
text.iast:
saṅkara suvana kesarī nandana |
teja pratāpa mahā jaga bandana ||

sanskrit: भवान् शङ्करस्य अवतारः, केसरी-पुत्रः च असि।
भवतः तेजः प्रतापः च महान् अस्ति, सम्पूर्णं जगत् भवन्तं वन्दते (नमति)॥
english: You are the incarnation of Shiva and the son of Kesari.
Your radiance and valor are immense, and you are revered by the whole universe.

boxes.title: The Radiance of Grounded Service
boxes.description: Shankara represents the highest spiritual intellect and ego-less discipline, while Kesari represents a highly practical, grounded, forest-dwelling leader. Hanuman embodies the perfect balance of both: he possesses the brilliant mind of a supreme thinker, yet uses his fierce protective energy (Teja Pratapa) entirely for the selfless service of others rather than personal gain. The world reveres him (Jaga Bandana) because he proves that true majestic radiance comes from balancing high-minded vision with practical, ego-less dedication to your community.

items: Phonetic Shifts: Sanskrit शङ्कर (Shankara) seamlessly shifts into the Awadhi संकर (Sankara) losing the palatal 'sh'. Likewise, वन्दन (Vandana) hardens into बंदन (Bandana) with the व → ब shift.

The Secret of सुवन (The Glide / श्रुति): If वन्दन becomes बंदन, why didn't सुवन become सुबन? The word सुवन comes from the Sanskrit root सू (to beget) plus the noun suffix अन. Saying सू and अन rapidly together naturally creates a soft 'w/v' sound as a breath-bridge (a Glide or व-श्रुति). Because this व is just a fluid phonetic bridge between two vowels—and not a heavy structural consonant—the Awadhi speakers kept it soft instead of hammering it into a hard ब.
